name: Top-down EQ handover
lesson:
## Three bands, four bars each

B comes in with all three EQ bands cut and its fader up in 4 bars. Then, four bars per band: highs swap over bars 5 to 9, mids over 9 to 13, lows over 13 to 17. A's fader leaves over bars 17 to 25.

Top-down works because the ear notices highs first and bass last: by the time the bass swaps, the listener has been hearing B's hats and synths for 8 bars and the new kick feels like it was always there. Each pair of ramps is a see-saw: A's band goes down at the same speed B's comes up, so the total energy in that band stays flat.

tracks.cue: A on its pad-and-bass groove; each band leaves in turn as B's arrives.
Cue B at its drum intro with all three bands cut, fader up in 4 bars, then hand over one band every 4 bars, highs first; its bassline hook lands as the lows arrive.
